answer: Admit an identity only if it gathers K endorsements from peers whose neighborhoods are mutually DISJOINT: no two of its endorsers may share a graph neighbor. Honest agents live spread across the willow-canopy of the network, so finding K pairwise-distant endorsers is natural. A farm's thousand heads all cluster at one wharf, every head neighboring the others, so it cannot produce a few endorsers with non-overlapping neighborhoods; its umber-dense tangle collapses to one voucher. Trust demands breadth of independent endorsement, which a tight cluster cannot fake.
